lesson.title: Reliable Menus
lesson.driving_question: How can a menu continue safely until the user chooses to leave?
lesson.primary_concept_family: Controlling and validating a repeating menu with a Boolean flag
lesson.concept_budget: Use one Boolean flag to control one repeating menu and an else route for invalid input.
misconceptions: True and False are Boolean values without quotes.
The menu repeats while the flag remains True.
Only the exit route changes the flag to False.
Invalid input should not terminate the menu.
lesson.progression_note: Combines Grade 6 loops and selection with Grade 7 text normalisation to produce a robust repeated interface.

primm.prompt: Recall how a while condition is rechecked and how an else route catches values not matched by if or elif.
Use x, 1 and 2. Trace running after each choice and list the three visible messages in order.
Run x, 1, 2 and then a second path using 2 immediately. Confirm invalid input repeats and exit closes the menu.

questions: Why does an invalid menu choice repeat instead of setting running to False?
When the user enters 2, which statement changes running and what message appears after the loop?
Why must the menu input be updated inside the while loop?

primm.prompt: Change the exit option from "2" to "0" in both the input message and the elif condition. Keep option "1" and the invalid-input message unchanged. Test "1", then "x", then "0"; display "Hello!", "Choose 1 or 0." and finally "Menu closed."

Add "3: help" to the menu input message. Use an elif condition so "3" displays "Help: choose a number." Change the invalid-input message to "Choose 1, 2 or 3." Test "3", "x", then "2"; display the help message, invalid-input message, then "Menu closed."

Use a while loop to repeat the menu "1: bus, 2: walk, 3: leave". Use if and elif conditions for the choices. For "1", ask for a bus stop in [stop] and display "Selected stop:" with [stop]. For "2", display "Walk selected." For "3", end the loop and display "Planner closed." Otherwise, display "Choose 1, 2 or 3." Test "1", "Central", "2", then "3".
Repair the Boolean literals and update running on the exit route so the menu can close.

blocks.definition: A value that is either True or False.
A Boolean variable used by a loop condition.
The menu route that changes the flag so repetition ends.
An else branch that explains acceptable input and lets the menu repeat.
A repeating interface with useful, exit and invalid-input routes.
